The chain used to build the state, for a one-run reproduction

7. POST /api/invoices/create {work_order_id}     -> 500 with no contact / 201 with one
Two adjacent server errors of the same shape, recorded but not claimed to share a cause
returns 500 once validation passes, rather than a 400. Request ids
All three are the same pattern — a missing or unresolvable prerequisite producing a 500 instead of a validation message.
25 work orders were created during this re-test, each tagged
in its tech story, and all were deleted and verified absent afterwards. One asset (

— its only contact — because the product's confirmation for choosing a contact writes it to the asset. That is recorded rather than reverted, since reverting would require clearing a field the product marks as required.
Where this expected behaviour comes from: nothing written down. Stating that plainly rather than dressing it up.

We checked the six report specifications and the stories under this epic, and none of them says what answer the system should give when an invoice is requested for a work order that has no contact set. The expectation in this ticket rests on consistency with the answers the product already gives for other missing prerequisites — for example "Work order is not complete." and "Line can`t be completed with unfulfilled part requests." — and on the general principle that a missing piece of required information should produce a clear rejection rather than a server error. That is a reasonable expectation, but it is our reading and not a quoted requirement.
This ticket is already closed. It is recorded here so that the record is honest about what the expectation rested on.

content.text: Re-tested 2026-08-04 — you were right that it did not reproduce, and the cause was not the canned line
Thank you for pushing back. Re-tested on the same branch and same build (

, checked at the start and again at the end — the branch has not moved, so nothing here is explained by a redeploy). The description above has been rewritten to match what actually happens. The ticket has been
pre-set jobs ("canned lines") available at Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and drove a work order end to end with

, covering every way a pre-set job can be priced — fixed labour, fixed line total, and an hourly rate — including the $0-value one and the one with no time estimate. Every attempt is named in the table in the Steps section.
. All eleven behaved identically. The thing that decides it is whether the work order has a
— the invoice is created normally, on every pre-set job tried.

I proved that by holding everything else still: same customer, same asset, same pre-set job, same steps, same money on both ($406.09). The only difference between the two work orders was the contact. The one without a contact failed; the one with a contact produced an invoice and moved to
Why you could not reproduce it.
Because the product stops you before you can. On a work order with no contact the
tab is greyed out and tells you exactly what to do —
"Please select a contact for the asset"

button on the screen at all. Pick a contact and everything works. Whichever pre-set job you used, your work order had a contact, so invoicing worked. There is a screenshot of each state on the ticket now.
Where my original report was wrong, plainly.

button on screen fails. It does not. I never actually pressed that button — I sent the request to the back end directly, which skipped the check the screen makes. I have corrected that in the description rather than leave it on the record.

Only this: if that request is sent straight to the back end for a work order with no contact, the back end answers with a general "something went wrong" server error instead of a clear message saying the contact is missing.
Nobody using the product can reach it
, and neither can a manual tester. It is the same pattern as two other back-end calls noted in the technical section.
Two things for you to decide, and I have not acted on either:
This ticket is closed (OBSOLETE / Done) and I have left it that way.
I changed only the description and added this comment — the status, resolution, priority, parent and both "blocks" links are untouched and byte-verified as unchanged. My recommendation is to
: there is no user-facing fault to fix.
. Per your standing instruction that anything reachable only by calling the back end directly must be raised with you first, I have
opened anything new for it. If you would like it raised as its own small ticket — "return a clear message instead of a server error when a work order has no contact" — say so and I will.
